claim: At grant, US4949039A lists inventor Peter Grünberg and is assigned to Kernforschungsanlage Jülich GmbH (later Forschungszentrum Jülich), documenting public-research-institute ownership of a multilayer magnetic-field sensor exploiting antiparallel ferromagnetic thin layers.
metric_value: Kernforschungsanlage Jülich assignee; Peter Grünberg inventorship
notes: Origin / ownership facts from the patent document. Not a commercial value amount and not an exact marketed HDD-head mapping.

claim: Baibich, Broto, Fert et al. (Phys. Rev. Lett. 61, 2472–2475, 1988-11-21) report giant magnetoresistance in (001)Fe/(001)Cr superlattices, with resistivity nearly halved in ~2 T for thin Cr spacers at 4.2 K — establishing a pre-T0 scientific GMR platform later applied to magnetic-field sensors / read heads.
notes: Pre-T0 scientific platform context for GMR. Not E3 product mapping and not patent-level attributable value for US4949039.

claim: Binasch, Grünberg, Saurenbach & Zinn (Phys. Rev. B 39, 4828(R), 1989-03-01) report enhanced magnetoresistance in Fe–Cr–Fe layered structures with antiferromagnetic interlayer exchange, much stronger than ordinary anisotropic magnetoresistance — establishing a pre-T0 Grünberg-group platform continuous with US4949039.
metric_value: Fe-Cr-Fe enhanced magnetoresistance with AF interlayer exchange (PRB 1989)
notes: Pre-T0 scientific continuity for the inventor's layered magnetoresistance work. Not a marketed GMR product mapping.

claim: The granted patent discloses a magnetic-field sensor stack of ferromagnetic layers with an intermediate nonferromagnetic layer arranged for antiparallel magnetization components, producing magnetoresistance changes substantially greater than anisotropic MR systems lacking antiparallel alignment / proper interlayer — a public device-architecture option signal for future high-sensitivity magnetic read sensors years before commercial GMR HDD heads.
value_carrier: aspirational multilayer GMR-type magnetic read-sensor / HDD-read platform (not a marketed GMR product at T0)
metric_value: antiparallel FM / non-FM multilayer magnetic-field sensor with enhanced MR vs anisotropic MR
notes: Package B option/future-value signal observable before IBM 1997 commercial GMR/spin-valve heads. Must not be read as R3 implementation in a marketed GMR HDD product at T0=1990-08-14. Contemporaneous ~1990 AMR MR heads are a different technology and are not treated as embodiment of this GMR patent.

claim: The granted patent claims a magnetic-field sensor with the specified antiparallel ferromagnetic multilayer stack and explicitly frames intended use for reading magnetically stored data (hard disks, floppy disks, magnetic tape) as well as other high-spatial-resolution magnetic-field measurement — claimed future device uses without a confirmed marketed GMR carrier at T0.
value_carrier: claimed magnetic-data-storage read-sensor modality (patent text; no marketed GMR carrier confirmed at T0)
metric_value: multilayer magnetic-field sensor for reading magnetically stored data / high-resolution field sensing
notes: Claimed/described future device uses support option-horizon interpretation. They are not proof that any marketed GMR HDD head embodied this exact patent at T0.
